subject: Prod path decision: hosting, audit evidence, and procurement owners
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elenap@carelogic.com>, Dr. Samir Rao <samir.rao@carelogic.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Prod path decision: hosting, audit evidence, and procurement owners

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the 45-minute call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment on constraints that will drive the deployment decision (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

Key constraints you called out:
- PHI in inference requests (clinical notes + identifiers) — must be covered under a BAA
- Internal security team requires SOC 2 Type II artifacts and a short evidence list for the audit intake (controls mapping + who to contact)
- Procurement prefers a single vendor that can commit to an SLA; they asked for cost guidance and procurement owner for an RFP

Initial qualification takeaways:
- Hosted API would be fastest to production but requires a BAA and may not meet your requirement for isolated GPU tenancy if you require dedicated hardware.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is our middle path: predictable throughput, tenant isolation, and we can surface token-level logs and retention controls that usually satisfy audit teams — still requires a signed BAA.
- Private VPC or on-prem solves most regulatory concerns but has longer lead time (networking, KMS/HSM integration, and acceptance testing).

Attachments (included): Redwood-BAA-onepager.pdf (summary), SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx (what security asks for), mutual-action-plan.docx (blank MAP).

Proposed next actions (please confirm owners and timelines):
1) CareLogic to confirm procurement contact (email) and an initial budget window (Procurement owner / this week)
2) Redwood to share a focused SOC2 artifact list mapped to your control questions (Karthik will own) — target: 48 hours
3) Decide path for POC: we recommend a 6-week Dedicated POC to validate throughput/privacy and to provide the exact artifacts your auditors need (if you want to evaluate Private, we can scope but it will add 4–6 weeks)

Can you confirm procurement contact and whether the CareLogic security team wants the artifacts directly or through your security portal?

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short MAP draft and a cost ballpark for the Dedicated POC.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Redwood-BAA-onepager.pdf)
(Attachment: SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx)

Subject: Re: Prod path decision: hosting, audit evidence, and procurement owners

Thanks Dylan — good summary. A couple quick notes: 

1) Procurement lead is procurement@carelogic.com (Amy Chen). I’ve looped them in.
2) Security prefers artifacts uploaded to our vendor portal (we’ll send an invite). In the meantime, the immediate artifact list we typically need is: BAA, SOC 2 Type II report (last 12 months), IAM diagram, data retention policy, and PII/PHI handling notes.
3) For timeline: security wants to run an initial intake this month; procurement is pushing for a commercial decision by end of November.

We’re open to a Dedicated POC if you can provide the artifact bundle quickly.

— Elena
Elena Park
Director of Product, CareLogic Health
(Attachment: vendor-intake-form.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elenap@carelogic.com>, Dr. Samir Rao <samir.rao@carelogic.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T12:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Prod path decision: hosting, audit evidence, and procurement owners

Elena — thanks. I’ll own the artifact push and the technical write-up. A few clarifications from the tech side to help you decide between Dedicated and Private: 

- Evidence we can provide immediately (48–72 hours): SOC2 Type II attestations summary, control mapping spreadsheet (controls -> Redwood evidence), network/architecture diagram, and data retention configuration options. We can also provide a redacted SOC2 report under NDA.
- Hosted API: supports short-retention logs (configurable) and BAA; recommended only if you do not require physical isolation.
- Dedicated: provides tenant-level isolation, fixed GPU pools, options for customer-managed KMS (if needed), and is the fastest way to satisfy both performance and most compliance asks. Latency & throughput SLOs are configurable under Dedicated contracts.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): recommended if your auditors require complete third-party isolation or you must install agents in your environment. This adds network/setup time and separate runbooks for ops and patching.

Suggested POC scope (Dedicated, 6 weeks):
- Week 0–1: Contract + BAA execution + access provisioning
- Week 2–3: Ingest sample traffic + validate latency and KV cache behavior
- Week 4: Security intake — provide artifacts to your portal and answer questions
- Week 5–6: Run edge cases, finalize performance numbers and a runbook for production cutover

I’ll prepare the control mapping and a small architecture diagram for the vendor portal. Dylan — I’ll drop the SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx and a short control mapping to the HubSpot deal and to Elena’s portal invite.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: SOC2-evidence-checklist.xlsx)

- For procurement: I can provide a commercial ballpark for the Dedicated POC and an estimate for a 12-month committed Dedicated plan (so you can include it in the RFP).
- For security: please add us to the vendor portal and list the single point of contact for each artifact request; Karthik and I will monitor and respond within 48 business hours.

Next suggested immediate steps:
1) Amy (procurement@carelogic.com) to confirm budget band and procurement timeline (by EOD 2027-11-05)
2) CareLogic security to send vendor portal invite; Karthik to upload control mapping and SOC2 excerpts (by 2027-11-04)
3) Dylan to share signed MAP + Dedicated POC SOW (we can use a short-term credit while contracts finalize)

I’ll attach the SOW draft to the HubSpot deal and follow up with a Loom that walks through the success criteria.

— Marissa
